title: Photography & Digital: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the exposure triangle — three settings that decide how a photograph looks.
meta_desc: GCSE foundations of photography: aperture, shutter speed, ISO and the exposure triangle.
final_note: Get the triangle balanced and any subject becomes possible.

concepts.def: Size of the lens opening, measured in f-stops.
How long the sensor is exposed to light.
Total light reaching the sensor for an image.
Aperture, shutter speed and ISO working together.
Aperture value — small f-number means wider opening.

walkthroughs.body_html: Aperture controls how wide the lens iris opens. A small f-number like f/1.8 is a wide opening — lots of light, shallow focus. A large f-number like f/16 is a narrow opening — less light, lots of focus front-to-back.

Shutter speed is measured in fractions of a second. A fast shutter like 1/1000 freezes movement; a slow shutter like 1/15 will blur it. Below about 1/60 you usually need a tripod to avoid camera shake.

Low ISO values like 100 or 200 give clean images in bright light. Raising ISO to 1600 or 3200 lets you shoot in dim conditions but introduces noise — grainy speckles. Start low and raise ISO only when you have to.
